title: Too small
summary: A big club's chief scout is coming on Saturday. Your dad knows the name: the man who told you at fourteen you were too small. He waits by the players' entrance. Dad still has the letter. A season on, the scout retires.

ends.title: He got it wrong
ends.text: The scout who said you were too small at fourteen told you to your face that he got it wrong. You said he did.

ends.title: The letter
ends.text: Your dad kept the letter that said you were too small. It's framed now, next to a photo of you, taller than the scout.

ends.title: Walked past
ends.text: The man who said you were too small waited by the players' entrance. You walked past him. He nodded, like he understood.

beats.title: The name

say: {agent.name}: "A big club's chief scout is coming Saturday. He asked for you by name. Says he's watched you for a year." He says the name. You know it.

replies.label: "He told me at fourteen I was too small."

small.text: "Ha. Then let him watch." When you ring your dad, he goes quiet, then goes to the loft.

fine.text: "That's the spirit." When you tell your dad the name, he says, "Oh," and nothing else.

beats.hint: Your agent has news about Saturday

beats.title: By the door

say: After the game, by the players' entrance. Your dad's come. A man in a big club's coat is waiting by the door, older than you remember. "That's him," your dad says. "He's shrunk."
He shakes it. "I got you wrong. I say that to maybe one player a year. You were fourteen and five foot one and I wrote 'too small'. I'm sorry."

past.text: He nods as you go by, as if he's had this before. Your dad walks past him too, very slowly.

did.text: "I did." He doesn't argue. He writes something in his notebook and you'd give a lot to know what.

grew.text: He laughs. "Not much." Your dad laughs too, which surprises everyone.

letter.text: "Course he did." The scout looks at your dad. Your dad looks back. Nobody says anything for a while.

beats.hint: Someone is waiting after the game

beats.title: The letter

event.title: The letter
event.speaker: dad
setup: Your dad turns up with a brown envelope from the loft. Inside, a letter from a big club, dated the year you were fourteen. Halfway down: "physically too small for our programme at this time."

outcomes.text: He's already bought the frame. It's in the car.

choices.label: Post it to the scout with a signed photo.

outcomes.text: You sign the photo "5 foot 11". A week later a card comes back: "Fair."
"I'll keep it," he says. "You can bin it when I'm dead." He puts it back in the envelope.

beats.hint: Dad's found something in the loft

beats.title: His last report

event.title: His last report
event.speaker: agent
setup: A season on. {agent.short} forwards a note: the scout has retired. He's sent you a photocopy of one page from his last notebook. Your name, a date, and one line.

outcomes.text: "Wrong at fourteen. Right now. Tell his dad." You take it round to your dad's. It goes in the frame, under the letter.
"Walked past me. Good for him." You read it twice.
"Got this one wrong. Glad I did." You read it three times.

choices.label: Send it to your dad without reading it.

outcomes.text: Your dad reads it to you down the phone. "He says good for you for walking past." Your dad sounds pleased about that.
Your dad rings you. He reads it out. Then he goes and gets the frame.
Your dad reads it out: "Got this one wrong." He says it twice, the second time for himself.

beats.hint: A season on, the scout retires
